..
Issued at 1252 PM CDT Sun Oct 18 2026

The cold front is currently extending over west central MN and 
southwestward though west central NE connected to a 982mb low over 
northeastern Manitoba/Hudson Bay. With the exception of 
east/southeast SD still ahead of the front, the rest of the CWA is 
in north to northeast flow with some gusty winds (20-35 mph) 
tracking right behind it, per weak CAA, over central SD to the James 
River. Downsloping winds off the Coteau will continue to diminish 
and finally end once the wind shifts to the northeast.

The ~1023mb high pressure will continue to slide in from the 
northwest, with the center over ND/MT/Canada border by 06Z. This 
high will remain dominant over the region Monday as we continue with 
dry conditions. Per this high and ongoing weak CAA, temps will be a 
few degrees cooler at any one location overnight than what we saw 
earlier this morning and around the same over the Coteau per 
inversion. Overall low temps are forecast to range in the upper 30s 
to the lower 40s. Probability of temperatures below 36 degrees (for 
frost formation) is 40-65% but spotty over north central and 
portions of northeastern SD (mainly along the ND/SD border and James 
Valley) per REFS/NBM. Probability of temps at 35 decrease a bit (20-
40%) for these areas with a 0% chance of temps dipping at 32 or 
lower. So patchy to areas of frost are in the grids for these areas 
with no freeze expected at this time. Highs for Monday will be the 
"coolest" of the week with temps ranging in the lower to mid 60s. 
This high will track east Monday with the CWA between this high and 
broad area of low pressure to our west Tuesday with ongoing dry 
conditions. Lack of any moisture in this dry air mass keeps the 
forecast dry through Thursday.

Looking at the pattern aloft by midweek, it will consist of 
southwest flow over the region as Clusters overall agree on a closed 
cutoff low developing over the Pacific and nearing the CA coast by 
Wednesday morning with a weaker open wave developing over the Gulf 
of Alaska. Due to this a broad ridge will build east of the Rockies, 
and really amplifying over the region Thursday, shifting eastward on 
Friday. Winds will be south/southeasterly at the surface and 
southwest at 850mb ahead of the low within the warm sector these 
days. This will also lead to a bit more moisture to return at lower 
levels as dewpoints are forecast to increase back into the 50s. 
Highs are forecast in the 70s, however, the 25-75th spread is 5-7 
degrees as we are several days out. Clusters indicate this southern 
cutoff low becomes an open wave as it tracks over the western CONUS 
Thursday with a bit of a difference in ensembles on whether these 2 
waves phase together or remain separate in split flow as the overall 
trough tracks east/northeast into the central and northern CONUS. 
With its developing surface low over the Northern Rockies Friday, 
models indicate the return of precip (30-50% NBM) Friday into 
Saturday as the low/cold front is forecast to strengthen as it 
tracks northeast in Canada Saturday. Models seem to have a good 
handle of this setup but exact placement and intensity of the 
surface low (and wave aloft) does vary a bit as GEFS indicates a 
stronger wave/sfc low with GEPS a bit weaker and ENS right in 
between. This results in low confidence of precip timing and QPF 
amounts which is why NBM pops are broadbrushed. Looking at the 
probability of or exceeding 0.25" per mean ensemble (GEFS/ENS/GEPS) 
is only about 25-35%. Again this is several day out, so 
probabilities for precip and QPF amounts will change.

With this incoming system/steeper pressure gradients ahead of the 
low will lead to winds increasing along and west River Thursday 
afternoon, with gusts up to 35 mph. Widespread stronger winds are 
forecast Friday as this low deepens with gusts potentially ranging 
from 35 to 45 mph Friday afternoon across the CWA with a prob of 
over 45 mph per NBM is 35-45% here and there for now. Relative 
humidity at this point looks to stay above 40% but with the lack of 
rain/dry air we have been dealing with and the warmup expected for 
the end of the week, the Grassland Fire Danger Index jumps into the 
High Category along and west River Thursday and High Category pretty 
much over the entire CWA Friday. This is still a few days away and 
mentioned above, depends on strength of low/pressure gradients which 
results in what the gusts will be, but this is something to watch 
for any elevated fire danger concerns.
